title: Latest historical cohort
text: In the 1998-09-01 snapshot there are 4,393 eligible accounts. The highest-risk 10% contains 440 accounts. Counts are accounts in one historical snapshot, not unique customers across all months.

title: Holdout model performance
text: Histogram Gradient Boosting achieved ROC-AUC 0.9227, PR-AUC 0.1983, and top-10% lift 7.08x. Targeting 1,318 of 13,177 test account-month observations captured 141 of 199 cases (70.85% recall). Precision was 10.70%. These metrics reproduce the fixed original model.

title: What disengagement means
text: Next-90-day customer activity at or below 60% of the same-snapshot median future/past activity ratio; eligible accounts have at least four previous-90-day customer-initiated transactions. The data has no observed account-closure label. The model predicts a severe decline in activity, not literal customer churn or credit default.

title: Model training and evaluation
text: The model used 100 features and 69,789 train-plus-validation account-month rows, with a fixed random seed and original hyperparameters. The test period is July–September 1998. Account IDs, dates, split labels, and target outcomes are excluded from predictive features. Risk scores are not calibrated probabilities.

title: Customer retention strategies
text: Common reactivation strategies include personalised communication, account health reviews, payment engagement campaigns, and product education. These are intervention hypotheses; the dataset does not show that these actions cause improved retention.

title: Campaign economics
text: Expected saves = targeted accounts × assumed precision × assumed save rate. Campaign cost = targeted accounts × contact cost. Break-even retained value per saved account = contact cost / (precision × save rate). If precision or save rate is zero, no finite retained value breaks even at positive contact cost. All currency values use an arbitrary common value unit.
source: Scenario model · assumptions, not observed effects

title: Research limitations
text: Historical cohort research, not current customer or credit-risk predictions. Risk scores rank behavioral disengagement; they are not calibrated probabilities. The fixed model and top-10% policy were selected in the original research. This is reproduction, not fresh holdout discovery. Snapshot features precede each snapshot. A stricter purged temporal robustness check removed training observations whose 90-day outcome windows crossed into evaluation periods; the purged locked test retained ROC-AUC 0.9202 and top-10% lift 6.63x. Campaign economics are assumptions and do not establish intervention effectiveness.

title: Dataset and provenance
text: This project uses the historical anonymized Berka / PKDD 1999 Czech financial dataset. Original transaction history spans 1993–1998. The source research reports 4,500 accounts and over one million transactions. Only aggregate analysis is published here; the account-level dataset remains local.
